correctness.rationale: For t>=2 the consecutive generalized Stern pair A_t,m,A_t,m+1 is coprime over every field: Bezout survives X->X^t and the pair recursion passes to (U,XU+V) and (XU+V,V). For any prime p dividing t, the derivative of odd-index A_t,2m+1 = XU+V reduces mod p to U=A_t,m(X^t), which is coprime to XU+V, so every odd-index monic polynomial has squarefree reduction and p-unit discriminant; in particular it is separable in characteristic zero. Any even n=2^r u gives A_t,n(X)=A_t,u(X^{t^r}), degree d=D t^r. Because constant coefficient is 1, its separable composition discriminant has abs value t^{r D t^r}|Disc A_t,u|^{t^r}; thus v_p(Disc)=r d v_p(t). Power-of-two n have polynomial 1 and are excluded. Independently reconstructed polynomials and exact gcd/discriminants with SymPy across t=2,3,4,5,6,9, dozens of nonconstant indices; all checked valuations match, finite tests not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Dilcher–Ericksen (2014), Propositions 19–20, prove the classical t=2 simple-root theorem and odd discriminants; these are explicit prior work. Their 2015 generalized-parameter paper Section 5, especially Propositions 5.1 and 5.4, covers limited cyclotomic square factors and selected index/parameter families, not arbitrary t,n or the exact p|t valuation law. The new uniform all-parameter result is not implied by those restricted statements, and the 2015 founding paper defines recurrences and coefficient/degree structure. There remains risk of later equivalent universal theorem.
residual_risks: Equivalent universal simple-root or parameter-prime discriminant formulas in unindexed post-2015 generalized Stern literature remain possible.
Only primes dividing t are classified; all other discriminant primes and splitting fields are unaddressed.

value.rationale: Simple-root classification across every generalized Stern parameter and index closes a natural known family of repeated-factor questions, explicitly extending earlier partial parameter/index results. The exact prime-divisor discriminant exponents identify arithmetic degeneration under even-index polynomial composition and provide precise p-adic information for prime factors of the parameter, while not claiming the complete discriminant.

limitations: Nonconstant polynomials only, t>=2; exact valuations only for p|t; no complete integer discriminant or root location.
Finite SymPy checks corroborate symbolic proof and are not universal verification.
